snippet.title: The Art of Irish Beekeeping: The Keepers | Honey Bee Documentary
snippet.description:
Set against the wild beauty of Ireland’s Beara Peninsula, this intimate documentary follows the De Ruiter family and their deep relationship with the honey bee after 25 years of life and beekeeping in Ireland. From pollen to pot, the film offers a poetic and immersive portrait of the apiary process, revealing how honey is shaped by landscape, season, family knowledge and the fragile rhythms of nature.

Through the family’s daily stewardship, the documentary explores the cultural folklore of bees, the urgent environmental challenges facing pollinators today, and the powerful role conscious human care can play in protecting the natural world. Interwoven with original music and poetry, the film journeys alongside the honey bee and its keepers, uncovering a story of resilience, adaptation, ecology and interdependence.

Both lyrical and grounded, this documentary is a moving celebration of Irish beekeeping, sustainable living, family tradition and the quiet intelligence of the honey bee.

snippet.title: What Happens When Money Becomes Worthless?
snippet.description:
Hyperinflation isn’t just about numbers—it destroys people’s lives.
In this short, we dive into the human side of hyperinflation:

Why paychecks lose value faster than people can spend them

How families are forced to sell belongings just to eat

Venezuela’s crisis, where salaries lost 90% of value in a single year

Why shortages of food, medicine, and essentials become normal

How people turn to bartering when money means nothing

The rise in crime and desperation as economies collapse

From Weimar Germany to Zimbabwe to Venezuela, the human cost of hyperinflation is measured in suffering, migration, and loss of hope.

Understanding this shows why inflation control is one of the most important roles of central banks and governments.

snippet.title: 6 Things People Bought Right Before Hyperinflation That Made Them Rich
snippet.description:
6 Things People Bought Right Before Hyperinflation That Made Them Rich  
 
What do people who survive hyperinflation do differently from those who lose everything?

This video breaks down real historical patterns from events like the Weimar Hyperinflation, Zimbabwe Hyperinflation, and Venezuelan Crisis—revealing the six types of assets that consistently preserved (and sometimes multiplied) wealth.

This isn’t theory.
It’s pattern recognition from a century of monetary collapse.

Inside this video, you’ll learn:

Why hyperinflation is more psychological than financial
The 6 asset categories that outperformed collapsing currency
How ordinary people—not experts—protected themselves early
The critical timing mistake that destroys most savers
The signals that appeared before every major currency collapse

From foreign currency and gold to real estate, inventory, and barter goods—these strategies appeared again and again across different countries and decades.

Most people wait for certainty.
By then, it’s already too late.

This video is not about fear.
It’s about understanding how systems behave when they fail—and what history teaches us about survival.

snippet.description:

- The 1980s Bubble Economy and the heights of Tokyo wealth.
- The 1985 Plaza Accord and the strengthening Yen.
- The 1990 market crash and the start of deflation.

snippet.title: Why LA’s mayor will never have much power #shorts
snippet.description:
With the election of Zohran Mamdani in New York City, big-city mayors have once again become a focal point of national politics. 

Now, in Los Angeles, the mayoral race in November is heating up with Councilmember Nithya Raman edging out reality TV star Spencer Pratt to secure her candidacy against incumbent Mayor Karen Bass. And Raman, a Democratic Socialist like Mamdani, is zeroing in on housing and affordability as defining issues of local politics.

But beneath the promises to take on hot-button issues that plague Angelenos, a persistent question remains: Why can’t the LA mayor get anything done?

Part of the answer takes us back to the creation of the LA city charter, a product of the turn-of-the-20th-century progressive movement that emerged in response to the corrupt politics that plagued cities like New York and Chicago.

Despite the radical and experimental origins of LA’s decentralized governance approach, a weak mayoral office may no longer be the best way to serve the people of Los Angeles today. Even if LA elected a progressive, Mamdani-esque candidate, the mayor’s office still has an uphill battle with fragmentation and decades of mounting red tape designed to favor negotiators over visionaries for mayor. #mayor #mamdani #losangeles

snippet.description:
Why do the world’s most powerful central banks still hold gold?
Even though the gold standard ended in 1971, countries continue to keep thousands of tons of gold in their vaults. If money is no longer backed by gold… why does it still matter?

In this video, we’ll unravel why central banks hold gold and why it remains one of the most important financial assets in the world today:

Why Gold Still Matters to Central Banks – trust, diversification, and liquidity

Gold isn’t used in daily transactions anymore, but it still provides trust, stability, and protection when currencies and markets face uncertainty. That’s why gold remains the ultimate reserve asset — even in a digital economy.
